rubric_items.reason: All four ticket acceptance criteria map to REQ-1, REQ-2, REQ-4 and REQ-5; job timing is listed under Out of scope with a reason.
Most REQs are atomic and checkable; REQ-6 merges the Cancelled and No-show cases, while REQ-4 and REQ-5 split the analogous cases.
Every known status cites the ticket or an IDE answer (A-01 to A-07), and the cited answers say what the artifact claims.
The Scheduled-only-can-change clash was asked (Q-03) and recorded as a mismatch, but the clash with glossary Cancelled ('before it took place') for past or Stale appointments is not recorded.
Questions Q-01 to Q-05 offered real options with defaults and were answered; none remain open needlessly.
Plain wording; glossary terms are used consistently, and 'reschedule' is tied to the glossary term 'move'.

findings.text: REQ-9 and REQ-6 let staff cancel an appointment after its start time, but the glossary defines Cancelled as called off before it took place. A-03's mismatch records only the glossary#scheduled clash, not this one.

cites.quote: Staff can still cancel a Stale appointment `with a reason`.
An appointment called off before it took place, with a reason
Mismatch: the glossary says only Scheduled appointments can change

findings.suggested_fix: Extend A-03's mismatch to cite glossary#cancelled and note that cancelling a past (Stale) appointment departs from the Cancelled definition.

findings.text: REQ-6 is compound: it covers two behaviours (Cancelled is not Stale; No-show is not Stale). A-05's options also treated them separately. REQ-4 and REQ-5 split the analogous Completed and rescheduled cases.

cites.quote: An appointment cancelled or marked No-show within the one day is no longer `Scheduled` and is not marked Stale.
- options: Yes, confirm | No-show still becomes Stale

findings.suggested_fix: Split REQ-6 into one REQ for Cancelled and one for No-show, each citing A-05.

cites.quote: closed by staff once its start time has passed
